title: Tutorial: Reading SDG Mapping Results
subtitle: A complete guide to interpreting your research analysis results
about_body: This tutorial walks you through reading and interpreting SDG mapping results for your research. Understanding these results is essential for spotting the strengths of your research portfolio and finding collaboration opportunities.

steps.title: Understand SDG Match Scores
steps.description: Each research article is displayed with a percentage score showing how strongly it maps to a particular SDG.
details: Score 80–100%: Very strong alignment with that SDG
Score 60–79%: Moderate alignment, relevant to several SDG aspects
Score 40–59%: Weak alignment, may only touch the topic indirectly

steps.title: Analyze the SDG Distribution
steps.description: The distribution chart shows how your research topics spread across the 17 SDGs.
details: Identify which SDGs dominate your research portfolio
Find research gaps for future topic development
Compare your distribution against global trends or other institutions
Use the year filter to see how your research focus evolves over time

steps.title: Interpret the Keywords
steps.description: The system extracts and maps keywords from research abstracts to the relevant SDGs.
details: Highlighted keywords show the most influential terms in the SDG score
Click a keyword to see its definition and usage context
Verify that your key terms are correctly detected
Add synonyms or term variations if needed to improve accuracy

steps.title: Use the Recommendations
steps.description: Based on the analysis, the system recommends ways to strengthen your research alignment with SDGs.
details: Follow the suggestions to broaden your research scope
Consider collaborating with researchers focused on related SDGs
Use the recommended references to reinforce your theoretical grounding
Adjust your methodology to align better with the target SDGs

example.title: Example Result Interpretation
example.article_title: Implementing Blockchain Technology for Transparent Sustainable Food Supply Chains
example.interpretation: This article shows strong alignment with SDG 9 (blockchain technology) and SDG 2 (food security), and moderate contribution to SDG 12 (supply chain sustainability).

mistakes.solution: A low score doesn't mean the research is worthless. Use it as a chance to identify SDG angles you haven't covered yet.
Quality research usually contributes to multiple SDGs. Explore every detected link.
Always check that the extracted keywords match your research context. Correct them when needed.
Use the time filter to see how your research focus evolves and align it with current SDG priorities.

resources.description: Latest global data for every SDG

cta_body: Put what you learned here into practice to interpret the SDG mapping results for your research
